$comment: WIN-272 (M4.6) mutation plan. Each row breaks ONE decision and names the suites that must
notice. The driver is scripts/run-win272-mutations.mjs and the ledger it writes is
THREE HAZARDS FROM THE PREVIOUS TRANCHE'S SWEEP ARE DESIGNED AROUND HERE, and all three are
in that tranche's own ledger as a control:
(1) `execSync('cmd | tail')` reports TAIL's exit status, so every mutation looked KILLED.
The driver runs the suite with no pipe and reads the child's own status.
(2) a source mutation of a package consumed through `dist/` mutates a file nothing reads.
`@platos/kernel` resolves to dist for `redis-streams` and `apps/core-api`, so every row
that mutates the kernel declares `rebuild` and the driver refuses to run without it.
(3) pnpm does not hand a child's output back on execSync's error object, so a failing-case
pattern written against ANSI bytes records a kill with no case name. The driver captures
stdio itself and matches on the runner's own plain text.
WHICH ROWS NEED A CONTAINER is declared per row, because a sweep that ran every row against
Docker would take an hour and one that ran none of them would leave the conservation refusal,
the trim boundary and the whole socket lane unmutated.

mutations.subject: the client's own duplicate suppression
mutations.breaks: a redelivery of the frame at exactly the last applied position is APPLIED again, which is the double-apply the acceptance forbids

mutations.subject: gap detection
mutations.find: if (frame.seq > expected) return { kind: "gap", missing: frame.seq - expected };
mutations.replace: if (false) return { kind: "gap", missing: frame.seq - expected };
mutations.breaks: a frame that skips ahead is applied, so a client renders a partial answer it believes is whole

mutations.subject: the reserved-field refusal
mutations.breaks: a payload field named `seq` overwrites the sequence ON THE WIRE, so the producer chooses the client's gap detection

mutations.subject: why a stream stopped
mutations.breaks: a `stream.offline` frame with no cursor of its own classifies as `severed` rather than `interrupted`, so the reader loses the fact that the SERVER let it go on purpose -- the one distinction an operator needs to tell a policy decision from a crash
mutations.$note: the first draft of this row replaced the whole `stream.offline` branch with `if (false)`, which the COMPILER refused rather than a case noticing. A type error is evidence the type layer holds, not evidence a case is watching, so the row was rewritten to a mutation that compiles and changes behaviour

mutations.subject: the cursor's control-character refusal
mutations.breaks: a stream id carrying a newline is encoded into an SSE `id:` line, which injects a field into every reader's byte stream

mutations.subject: the length-prefixed cursor
mutations.breaks: the delimiter reappears between the id and the sequence, so an id holding the delimiter decodes to the wrong position

mutations.subject: M0.4 decision D4 AS CORRECTED
mutations.breaks: an absent `sv` defaults to 1 on a NEW surface too, which is the uncorrected proposal and makes the version field optional everywhere

mutations.subject: the per-frame byte ceiling
mutations.breaks: a frame of any size is admitted, so one tool result becomes a memory incident in every connected browser

mutations.subject: whether a client reconnects
mutations.breaks: a client polls a finished stream forever, because a completed turn is reported as resumable

mutations.subject: THE CONSERVATION REFUSAL
mutations.breaks: a cursor whose frames were trimmed is answered with a PAGE, so the client receives a gap dressed as a sequence and renders state that is silently missing the middle

mutations.subject: the trim boundary, off by one
mutations.breaks: a reader that is exactly caught up is REFUSED, so every reader at the boundary is disconnected instead of served

mutations.subject: no frames after a terminal frame
mutations.replace: if (seal !== null && false) return { kind: "sealed", seal };
mutations.breaks: a producer can append after the seal, which is the trailing-invalid-frames case the acceptance forbids

mutations.subject: the first seal wins
mutations.find: const set = await client.hsetnx(key, field, value);
mutations.replace: const set = await client.hset(key, field, value);
mutations.breaks: HSET OVERWRITES where HSETNX claims: a second seal replaces the first and still reports `already-sealed`, so a retry turns a completed turn into a failed one AND tells the caller it did not

mutations.subject: the length bound
mutations.find: await client.xadd(key, "MAXLEN", maxLength, entryId(entry.seq), ENTRY_FIELD, entry.body);
mutations.breaks: one runaway stream is unbounded, so a single turn can evict every other stream's frames from the server

mutations.subject: reads are STRICTLY after the cursor
mutations.breaks: a resuming reader is handed the frame it already holds, which is a duplicate on every reconnect

mutations.subject: at-least-once delivery
mutations.find: // THE POSITION IS NOT ADVANCED, which IS the redelivery. Break so
mutations.replace:
position = entry.id;
              // THE POSITION IS NOT ADVANCED, which IS the redelivery. Break so
mutations.breaks: a handler that rejects never sees the event again, so a partial failure silently loses it

mutations.subject: a fan-out seam is not a queue
mutations.breaks: a subscriber catches up on events published before it existed, which makes the bus a second canonical store beside the outbox

mutations.subject: the handshake wait, per command
mutations.breaks: a command issued on an ENDED client no longer waits and no longer fails closed, so a dead connection reports success paths it cannot serve

mutations.subject: backpressure
mutations.breaks: a full socket is written to without bound, so a slow browser becomes unbounded heap in this process

mutations.subject: THE CREDENTIAL EXPIRY FENCE
mutations.breaks: a stream outlives the credential that opened it by a day, which is the unbounded case the live lane has

mutations.subject: at most ONE terminal frame
mutations.breaks: a completed stream gets a SECOND terminal frame after the producer's own, which is the duplicate the acceptance forbids and the exact defect in `streaming.service.ts`

mutations.subject: the tenancy boundary IS the journal key
mutations.breaks: a stream id becomes a bearer capability across environments, so naming one environment reaches another's frames

mutations.subject: the scope is the AUTHORIZATION's, never the path's
mutations.breaks: a forged scope is honoured, because the key is built from the caller's own path segment rather than from the scope tenancy re-derived
mutations.$note: the two are equal on a well-formed request, so ONLY a forged-scope case can tell them apart; that is the point of the row

mutations.subject: encode, then write, then advance
mutations.breaks: a frame that was not written advances the position, so a resuming client is handed the frame AFTER the one it never received

mutations.subject: a terminal frame a client will APPLY
mutations.breaks: the terminal frame is numbered 0, which every correct client's `admitFrame` calls a DUPLICATE and drops — leaving it with no explanation for a stream that stopped
